scope: Independent read-only review of the exact v2 helper, private NSS config and supplied v2 probe; supported canonical first-argument shapes only.

findings.detail: Lines 5-8 route audit, pip sync and pip install into the private NSS branch. Other supported canonical commands use direct exec. Global-option-prefixed command forms are not covered.

Quoted $uv and $@ preserve arguments in both paths. The child consumes only the NSS pathname with shift, then execs the original uv argv. Both layers use exec; set -eu fails closed on namespace/mount failure without direct fallback. Probe records version/sync/audit exits 0 and invalid pip install argv exit 2. /bin/sh -n returned 0.

No argv rewriting, environment overrides, audit substitution, TLS relaxation or hash bypass. Receipt retains --require-hashes for the successful 20-package sync and --locked for the actual 37-package audit. Existing uv performs validation and determines its exit status.

Unshare creates a private-propagation mount namespace before binding the supplied NSS file and remounting the bind read-only. Config contains hosts: files dns myhostname; its current hash matches the probe. Reported host NSS before/after hashes are identical: fe9f1ec41fd85c042627670712732c0818d25b4b20051aad1bf987bdf43f06b6. No fresh live-host readback was performed.

Helper targets only the fixed development-tool uv executable; no product/runtime UID override or product configuration edit exists here. --map-root-user gives the tool child namespace-visible UID 0 mapped to the invoking host UID, not host root. Extending dispatch reuses this mapping; product runtime identity was not independently inspected.

verification.method: Static source/config review, local hashing, shell syntax check and parsed receipt validation only; no network, helper execution, generic harness, repository survey or Git operations.

limitations: The v1 approval does not approve v2; this verdict is independently bound to the three hashes above. No predecessor bytes were reread to establish a historical four-line-only diff or config baseline.
Probe results are supplied execution evidence, not new reruns. Its uv executable hash was not independently rehashed outside the allowed files.
A mount/user namespace is not a hostile-code or network sandbox; package operations retain their normal effects.
Fresh migration-fixture rerun and canonical-suite PASS remain uncredited, as do broader product/runtime acceptance claims.
